record.paper_title: Quantum Communication: From Fundamentals to Recent Trends, Challenges and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can quantum transport-layer congestion control avoid discarding entangled states and quantum data, given that setting up end-to-end entanglement is already difficult and discarded quantum information cannot be recreated because of the no-cloning theorem?

evidence.quote: The main open problems and challenges for developing fully-functional protocols in this layer for quantum internet include: 1. The current transport layer protocols discard entangled states and quantum data under congestion.

This is not useful from two perspectives. First, given the current limitations of the lower layers, setting up end-to-end entanglement is a challenge. Second, discarding entanglement and quantum information may lead to precious data loss, as quantum states cannot be recreated, because of the property of no-cloning theorem. Therefore, research should be done to find alternatives to discarding the entangled quantum states in the transport layer.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (2024–2025) on quantum internet protocol design explicitly identify transport-layer congestion control without discarding entanglement as an unresolved challenge. Works such as the Quantum ECN survey, "Leveraging Internet Principles to Build a Quantum Network" (2024), and "Quantum Internet: Technologies, Protocols, and Research Challenges" (2025) discuss partial proposals (cross-layer design, fidelity-threshold discarding, entanglement-ID schemes, packet-quantum intercommunication protocols) but no fully satisfactory protocol has been established. The problem appears to remain open with only partial mitigations proposed.

status_evidence.title: Quantum ECN and Beyond: A Survey on Congestion Control for Distributed Quantum
status_evidence.snippet: Congestion control in QDCs must balance fidelity-versus-throughput trade-offs; classical retransmission is forbidden by the no-cloning theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Congestion control for quantum networks is an active, unresolved research area with only partial mitigations.

status_evidence.title: Leveraging Internet Principles to Build a Quantum Network
status_evidence.snippet: Classical network mechanisms assume duplication of information, which is impossible in quantum networks due to no-cloning and monogamy of entanglement.
status_evidence.claim: Designing transport-layer mechanisms compatible with no-cloning is identified as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Protocols for Packet Quantum Network Intercommunication
status_evidence.snippet: EPR pairs cannot be retransmitted upon loss because of the no-cloning theorem; packet loss handling remains a fundamental issue.
status_evidence.claim: Loss handling without discarding entanglement remains a fundamental open issue.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Internet: Technologies, Protocols, and Research Challenges
status_evidence.snippet: Cross-layer co-design of link, network, and transport layers for quantum networks is needed and is currently lacking.
status_evidence.claim: A fully-functional quantum transport layer with congestion control that avoids discarding entanglement is still being researched.
